title: Identity lifecycle controls: reauth grace periods and session boundary enforcement
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: As Redwood ramps up RBAC v2 and stricter audit logging, we need clear session lifecycle semantics for SSO/SAML flows. Existing tickets covered basic JIT provisioning and MFA behavior, but we need a cohesive implementation that: (1) supports configurable re-auth (reauth) policies per-org and per-admin role; (2) defines a reauth grace window for 'expected' MFA that doesn't immediately block UX but records and escalates via audit logs; (3) enforces logout propagation across browser sessions and refresh-token rotation; and (4) emits a consistent set of audit events for downstream compliance.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admins can set an org-level 'reauth_policy' and 'reauth_grace_minutes' via the admin console or API.
2) Session enforcement modes supported: 'soft' (allow but log), 'hard' (block access until reauth), and 'timed' (allow within grace window then require).
3) JIT provisioning remains idempotent and records SSO_JIT_PROVISION audit events with subject, source_id, and attributes.
4) Logout triggers immediate session revocation server-side and emits SSO_LOGOUT_BROADCAST to all active devices; refresh token rotation/blacklist is verified.
5) MFA expectations: behavior documented and implemented for three states: 'not_expected', 'expected', 'required'. 'expected' should prompt on sensitive routes and generate MFA_PROMPTED logs but not fail existing sessions within grace window.
6) Audit logs include normalized event types and reason fields and are queryable in the Console's security view.
7) Unit + integration tests and end-to-end QA in a dev org demonstrate rollback and canary rollout to 10% of production traffic.
proposal:
High-level approach:
- Policy model: extend RBAC v2 org config with two keys: 'sso_reauth_policy' (soft|hard|timed) and 'sso_reauth_grace_minutes' (integer). Admins and role-scoped overrides supported via RBAC v2.
- Session tokens: keep short-lived access tokens (~15m) + rotating refresh tokens; server-side session index to allow immediate revocation on logout.
- SAML specifics: honor SessionNotOnOrAfter when present; map InResponseTo to our session index for logout binding. If session timestamps conflict with org policy, enforce the stricter (shorter) boundary.
- JIT provisioning: merge incoming attributes into identity graph; do not create duplicate accounts. Emit SSO_JIT_PROVISION event that includes attribute schema version.
- MFA semantics: add an 'mfa_state' attribute on sessions ('not_expected'|'expected'|'required'). 'expected' sets a flag that surfaces UI nudges and triggers MFA_PROMPTED logs on sensitive API calls. 'required' forces reauth immediately.
- Audit events: standardize payloads and forward to existing audit pipeline. New event types: SSO_JIT_PROVISION, SSO_SESSION_ESTABLISHED, SSO_SESSION_REAUTH_REQUIRED, SSO_SESSION_REAUTHED, SSO_LOGOUT_BROADCAST, MFA_PROMPTED, MFA_ENFORCED.
- Rollout: feature flag + canary in dedicated region, metrics for reauth-fail-rate, login-latency, customer API error increase.
tradeoffs:
- Soft-mode improves UX but weakens instant compliance guarantees; mitigated via audit and faster opt-in enforcement.
- Server-side session indexing adds memory/lookup cost but is necessary for immediate logout propagation. We'll use a TTL-backed index with sharded caches.
- Honoring SAML SessionNotOnOrAfter may shorten our preferred session length; we choose the stricter of org and SAML assertions to minimize divergence.
implementation_notes:
- Database: small session index table with session_id -> active boolean, org_id, mfa_state, created_at, last_activity. TTL-based cleanup.
- API: admin endpoints to read/write reauth policy; SDK-compatible responses for SDKs to surface 'reauth_required' hints.
- Console: new Security > Sessions view filters for 'requires reauth' and 'recently revoked'.
- Tests: add unit tests for mapping SAML attributes -> identity, integration tests for logout fanout across devices, and sim tests for grace windows.
- Observability: add metrics: sso.reauth.prompt.rate, sso.reauth.enforced.rate, sso.logout.broadcasts, session.revocations.count.
